exact_source_findings: Event.id is created when the immutable Event model is instantiated; parent_id may still be None at that point.
ConversationState.append_event performs the authoritative _stamp_parent_id(event) immediately before EventLog.append, then advances leaf_event_id/head_is_empty after the event file write.

LocalConversation's outer _tree_stamping is only a convenience stamp: UserPromptSubmit hooks can replace a MessageEvent after that outer stamp. The replacement constructor does not preserve id, timestamp, or parent_id, so an R7 marker created before hooks would bind the wrong event identity/lineage. The marker seam therefore has to be inside ConversationState.append_event after its authoritative stamp and before EventLog.append.

HookEventProcessor can synchronously emit HookExecutionEvent values through original_callback before the outer ActionEvent/MessageEvent reaches original_callback. Because those nested events are appended inside the same outer ConversationState context, multiple event files can be durable before the single deferred base_state save. A one-event marker is therefore insufficient; R7 requires a consecutive pending-event chain journal.
ConversationState.__exit__ writes the dirty base snapshot at the outermost state context, even when the context exits with an exception.

EventService.start claims the conversation lease before _scrub_persisted_credentials, constructs LocalConversation only later, and injects the ConversationState/EventLog write guard after construction. Pending-event recovery therefore has to be the first conversation-state operation immediately after lease claim, before credential scrub and before LocalConversation construction, or stale base_state can be rewritten before repair.

ConversationLease.guarded_write holds the lease lock while checking owner/generation and during the yielded disk write. Marker/base recovery and marker cleanup can therefore be fenced by the same generation on the agent-server local-filesystem path.

candidate_protocol.marker_path: one fixed pending-event commit journal per conversation; exact final path TBD in patch
candidate_protocol.prepare_event_seam: Inside ConversationState.append_event, after _stamp_parent_id and immediately before EventLog.append, invoke a private pre-append hook configured by agent-server. The hook atomically writes/extends the pending journal under the current lease guard.
chain_entry: sha256 of the exact event JSON bytes EventLog is about to write
candidate base_state JSON payload after deterministic append_event HEAD bookkeeping and, for a real user MessageEvent, last_user_message_id bookkeeping
sha256 of that candidate base payload
common_marker_fields: sha256 of the raw base_state.json present before the first event in the unsaved chain
optional exact-save payload and sha256, populated at base-save time
candidate_protocol.base_save_upgrade: In ConversationState._save_base_state, serialize the payload once. Before writing base_state, invoke a private pre-base-write hook that upgrades the existing journal with that exact serialized payload and digest; then write that same payload. Only after a successful base write invoke the post-base-write hook that removes the marker. This avoids false mismatch from Fernet's randomized ciphertext because the journal and base write share exactly the same serialized bytes.
startup_first_operation_recovery: Claim lease and obtain current generation.
Before credential scrub or LocalConversation construction, read the marker, raw base_state, and the marker-bound event files under the lease guard.
Require a well-formed marker from a strictly older generation for takeover recovery; same-generation same-owner retry remains a separate liveness policy decision and is not accepted by the model.
Verify that marker entries correspond to an exact consecutive prefix of event files. Digest, event id, parent, non-prefix presence, malformed chain, or base conflict fails closed.
If zero marker events exist and raw base digest is the recorded old digest, this is marker-before-event crash: remove marker only.
If an exact event prefix exists but base-save phase never started and raw base is still old, write the last present entry's candidate base payload, then remove marker.

If the journal contains an exact-save payload, require every journal event to exist. If raw base is old, write the journal's exact-save payload; if raw base already has its exact digest, cleanup only; any other base fails closed.
Never infer/adopt a markerless orphan event. A marker-bound event may coexist with older markerless orphan siblings because the marker, not unique-descendant structure, carries commit intent.

why_chain_not_single_marker: HookExecutionEvent emissions can be nested before the outer hooked event and all append inside one deferred state-save context. A fixed marker that only describes the latest event loses the recoverable prefix when a crash occurs after an earlier nested event is durable but before the next event write. The journal keeps per-event candidate snapshots so recovery can commit the exact durable prefix.
fernet_boundary: Cipher.encrypt uses Fernet.encrypt, which is randomized. Therefore precomputing a final encrypted base JSON and later comparing it to a separately reserialized successful base write is unsound. The candidate upgrades the journal with the exact payload bytes produced by _save_base_state immediately before writing those same bytes.
